title: A Finite Field Realisation of the Riemann Hypothesis
content: We give a comprehensive finite-field realisation of the Riemann Hypothesis within the Finite Ring Continuum framework, where arithmetic is carried by a finite relational symmetry shell. The decisive fact is that on the shell the quarter-turn meridian constitutes a complete spectral representation domain, and the half-turn 1/2 is at once the unique self-dual locus Tr=1, the self-adjointness symmetrizer of the scale-evolution generator \(H_h=-i(x\partial_x+\half)\), and the critical real part. In this spectral representation the real placement is fixed by the half-turn; the remaining datum is the height/order of the mode, not an additional real coordinate in the classical plane. The finite zeta zeros are the whole nonterminal spectrum of the Carrier shell, so the question is not \emph{where} they lie, but in what order they rebuild the prime-counting vector. We establish that spectrum from the prime side, as the scale-spectrum of the von Mangoldt comb, as the discrete roots of the secular condition \(\mathcal N(T)\in\Z-\half\) (recovered to \(4\times10^{-5}\)), and as the roots of an explicit companion matrix built from the comb. Unconditionally this reduces the hypothesis to a single clause: the completeness of the on-line spectrum for the prime vector, equivalently the faithfulness of the de-framing, in finite-shell Hilbert-P\'olya form. The strong RH claim is conditional on the reductio argument against the ontological infinity, under which no continuum exists beyond the shell. An off-line zero of a single Euler product is not refuted but unrealisable, i.e. the finite ontology holds no slot for a real part other than the self-dual one, making the placement on \(\Real=\half\) a construction identity. The generalized hypothesis is attained through the $\chi$-twist, and becomes a theorem of the framework.
